articleTitle: Adaptive torque control of hip exoskeleton for walking assist based on motion comparison method and phase oscillator method
publicationTitle: 2019 Intelligent Rehabilitation and Human-machine Engineering Conference (IRHE-2019)
abstract: This paper presents comparison of two torque control methods for walking assist applied to hip exoskeleton. One method is based on motion sequences comparison and Finite State Machine (FSM) and another method is based phase oscillator. Both methods can recognize walking intention (hip joint flexion and extension) well through simulation results. The human-robot dynamic system was modelled and adaptive torque control is analysed and simulated for walking assist hip exoskeleton torque control. With parameters tuned properly through simulation, volunteers experiment was conducted and results shows that both methods can help improve walking speed and stride well. Motion comparison method performs better during static state (suddenly stop during walking) while phase oscillator method can 100% recognize walking intention and provide compatible torque assist. An average walking speed improvement of 20.16% is detected by 10m ground level walking tests with hip exoskeleton compared to freely walking.

articleTitle: Low intensity pulsed ultrasound stimulation at different number of tone-burst on multi-scale coupling
publicationTitle: 2019 Intelligent Rehabilitation and Human-machine Engineering Conference (IRHE-2019)
abstract: In this paper, We used low-intensity pulsed ultrasound stimulation (LIPUS) on the motor cortex of mice and regulated the number of tone-burst (NTB) of LIPUS. The local field potential (LFP) signals of motor cortex and EMG signals of tail muscles were recorded simultaneously (NTB = 100,150,200,250,300). The synchronous characteristics and coupling strength of LFPs and EMG before and after stimulation with different NTB parameters were investigated by multi-scale transfer entropy(MSTE) analysis. The local field potential (LFP) signals of motor cortex and EMG signals of tail muscles of mice were multi-scale. The transfer entropy between LFP and EMG under different scale factors was calculated, and the nonlinear EEG coupling characteristics in different coupling directions (LFP-EMG and EMG-LFP) were obtained. Different parameters at the same scale are compared. The samples of mice were statistically analyzed. The results show that the coupling strength decreases first, then increases and then decreases with the increase of scale. And the coupling peak value changes with the change of NTB. Next, we will introduce the disease model into the study of low intensity pulsed ultrasound stimulation.

articleTitle: Multifractal analysis of joint flexion in elderly with the history of falls
publicationTitle: 2019 Intelligent Rehabilitation and Human-machine Engineering Conference (IRHE-2019)
abstract: In order to reduce the incidence of falls in the elderly, this paper studies the differences of the flexion angles of the arms, knee joint and ankle joint in the elderly. 39 elderly people in a community in Beijing were selected and their basic information (age, height, gender, etc.), history of diseases and falls were collected through questionnaires. According to the number of falls, they were divided into with-fall groups and no-fall groups. Biomechanical experiments were carried out in the limited space of the laboratory. The Timed Up and Go (TUG) experiment was carried out at free speed, and the kinematics data were collected by the motion capture system. This paper uses multifractal algorithm to analyze the parameter differences between different groups. The experimental results show that the position stability of knee joint is worse in the elderly with a history of falls; the fractal characteristics of flexion angle curve of arm and ankle joint of the two groups are weak. It is suggested that the knee joint should be intensively trained in daily life for the elderly with the history of falls.

articleTitle: System design of upper limb sEMG real-time control manipulator
publicationTitle: 2019 Intelligent Rehabilitation and Human-machine Engineering Conference (IRHE-2019)
abstract: In order to help people with hand deficiency return to society better, surface electromyogram signal (sEMG) of upper limb was used as signal source to realize real-time control of manipulator. First, we built upper limb sEMG acquisition circuit, using it to collect right forearm flexor carpi ulnaris and radial wrist extensor sEMG respectively. Then, sEMG training platform was bulit with MATLAB and C# mixed programming to achieve sEMG off-line training. When training completed, we exported weights and thresholds of BP neural network for achieving real-time control manipulator. Experimental result showed that accuracy of real-time control manipulator was higher than 92% after training and average recognition time was about 290ms, which meet time requirement within 300ms of prosthetic control field.

articleTitle: Influence of prosthetic weight on muscle fatigue in upper limb amputees
publicationTitle: 2019 Intelligent Rehabilitation and Human-machine Engineering Conference (IRHE-2019)
abstract: Wearing a myoelectric prosthesis is the most effective way to restore the lost limb functions for amputees in their daily life. Unfortunately, the control performance of myoelectric prostheses is commonly affected by a number of factors that limit their practical use. When most of the factors have been investigated in the previous studies, it remains unclear how muscle fatigue negatively affects the prosthetic control stability. In this pilot work, our goal was to study the muscle fatigue that was induced by wearing a prosthesis with different weights. The effect of the weight of the prosthesis on muscle fatigue was estimated by surface electromyography (sEMG) signals that were recorded from residual limb muscles of a transradial amputee before and after wearing the prostheses. Three features, mean absolute value (MAV), mean frequency (MNF) and median frequency (MDF), were extracted from the EMG recordings and then the maximum voluntary contraction (MVC) was represented by the MAV and the muscle fatigue tendency was estimated from the MDF and MNF. The preliminary results of the study indicated that the greater the weight of the prostheses, the more likely it was to cause muscle fatigue. Importantly, our results showed that the muscles of intact limb recover much quicker than the disabled side from muscle fatigue. This study could provide the guidance for amputees to select a proper prosthesis base on individual load capacity, and decide appropriate usage time in daily training activities.

articleTitle: Flexible non-contact electrodes for minimizing artifacts in electrocardiograms measurement during motion
publicationTitle: 2019 Intelligent Rehabilitation and Human-machine Engineering Conference (IRHE-2019)
abstract: The Electrocardiogram (ECG) is a critical physiological indicator that contains abundant information about human heart activities. It is a challenge to measure ECG signals, which is susceptible to interference from various types of noise. Generally, the signals are often detected by wet electrodes needing moist conductive gel to reduce the skin-electrode interface impedance, which could cause discomfort of the user and even lead to distortion of the signals due to the drying of conductive gel. In this study, a non-contact electrode that does not need any conductive gel nor ohmic connection with the skin was presented to apply high-quality physiological signals. It was made up of flexible printed circuits materials and the surface signal can be obtained by the principle of capacitive coupling. The results showed that the proposed non-contact electrode could acquire high-quality ECG compared to wet Ag/AgCl electrode. The correlation coefficient of the ECG waveforms was as high as 98.10% in the quiet state and 90.80% in the motion state between standard electrode and our non-contact electrode. The electrode was capable of obtaining good ECG signals even when the subject was walking at a speed up to 6 km/h. This pilot study suggests that the proposed flexible non-contact electrode would be a potential tool for long-term healthcare monitoring for patients and physiological signal measurements for athletes.

articleTitle: Functional corticomuscular coupling—interaction strength and information flow following stroke
publicationTitle: 2019 Intelligent Rehabilitation and Human-machine Engineering Conference (IRHE-2019)
abstract: The functional corticomuscular coupling (FCMC) between the cortex and the contralateral muscle can reflect and assess the motor function in sensorimotor system. Considering the inherently highly nonlinear and directional biological systems, the transfer entropy (TE) technique was applied to quantitatively analyze the functional connection between electroencephalogram (EEG) and surface electromyogram (EMG), while EEG over the scalp and EMG from flexor digitorum surerficialis / extensor digitorum were recorded simultaneously during performing grip task with steady-state force in nine stroke patients and nine healthy controls. The results showed that the interaction strength on stroke-affected hand was weaker in comparison with that on the unaffected hand and healthy controls. There, however, were no significant differences between two directions for stroke patients, while the FCMC in descending pathway was dominant at high beta-band (25–35Hz) than that in ascending direction for healthy controls. These differences might derive from the structural lesion which may disorder the function of oscillation, coordination, feedback and transmission between the efferent control and the afferent feedback. This study suggests that the FCMC between the brain and the contralateral muscle in interaction strength and information flow can be estimated by the TE method.

articleTitle: Data structures influence the number of muscle synergies and reconstruction effect across trials
publicationTitle: 2019 Intelligent Rehabilitation and Human-machine Engineering Conference (IRHE-2019)
abstract: Muscle synergy analysis featured with low dimensions was implemented extensively to operate neural control and rehabilitation assessment. Several researches suggested that the synergy number could be used as a physiological marker of motion deficiency, like the stroke and cerebral palsy children. However, it was still vague that the impact of data structure on synergy dimensionality, which was a fundamental question to be addressed and to help us better use the synergy number as an assessment metric. Therefore, we extracted synergies from three structures of electromyogram (EMG) using Nonnegative Matrix Factorization Algorithm (NNMF), including single-trial EMGs (SIN), average (AVE) and concatenation of all-trial EMGs (CON). Results indicated the significant impact of data structures on synergy numbers. Further, we also calculated the reconstruction effect of EMGs across trials to examine ability of the three structures to capture trial-based features. It suggested that synergies extracted by SIN captured more features of the original trial than other trials, and CON and AVE could both invariably and adequately reconstruct EMGs of four trials but with higher extent of CON than AVE. These results were beneficial in guiding synergy-based researches in rehabilitation assessment and control to deal with EMGs of multiple trials.

articleTitle: Research on neural activation mechanism of motor imagery based on virtual scene
publicationTitle: 2019 Intelligent Rehabilitation and Human-machine Engineering Conference (IRHE-2019)
abstract: Research have confirmed that specific virtual scenes in virtual rehabilitation can promote positive activation of motor imagery nerve. In order to analyze the changing trend of the activation characteristics of motor imagery neurons in different virtual scenes. In this study, six subjects were collected for 7 consecutive days of motion-imagining EEG signals in the control group (arrow scene), static (text and picture scene), dynamic (3D scene and virtual game) scenes. In subsequent analysis, the wavelet packet method was introduced to analyze the characteristics of motion regions. In this study, the α/β band was extracted to perform the power spectrum estimation and analyze the ERD/ERS characteristics. Finally, multi-level dynamic features of time, frequency and space domain were extracted and used to classify left-handed and right handed imaginary patterns by PSO-SVM model and to compare the change of recognition rate in different scenarios. The results showed that the motor cortical nerve activation area could be significantly expand by virtual scene training, and the contralateral dominant ERD in the α/β band was enhanced. In addition, the recognition of motion imagination based on dynamic virtual scenes is higher than that in static scenes. This study also provides a theoretical foundation for the virtual scene design strategy of the MI-BCI system.

articleTitle: Central aortic pressure waveform estimation using genetic-algorithm-based multichannel blind system identification
publicationTitle: 2019 Intelligent Rehabilitation and Human-machine Engineering Conference (IRHE-2019)
abstract: Central aortic pressure (CAP) has been reported to be a more clinically relevant marker for reflecting cardiovascular status and predicting cardiovascular risk than peripheral arterial pressure (PAP). Whereas, the direct measurement of CAP is invasive. Multichannel blind system identification (MBSI) provides a method for noninvasive CAP estimation from two or more PAP waveforms such as brachial and femoral pulse waves. However, most previous MBSI methods require the prior knowledge and manual searching for unknown model order, which greatly influence the accuracy of the CAP estimation. In this paper, we employed a genetic algorithm (GA) method for automatically identifying the model orders and parameters in MBSI technique to improve the accuracy of CAP estimation. The performance of the proposed GA-MBSI algorithm was evaluated in comparison with three previous MBSI methods. Preliminary experimental results using data from three Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats showed that the proposed GA-MBSI algorithm could provide an improvement on estimating the beat-to-beat systolic pressure (SBP), mean arterial pressure (MAP), and total waveform (TW) of the CAP with root mean square error (RMSE) of 2.02+0.76 mmHg, 0.30+0.14 mmHg, and 1.30+0.38 mmHg, respectively. In comparison to the three previous MBSI methods, the proposed method efficiently reduced the RMSE of SBP, MAP and TW of the estimated CAP by at least 9.42%, 34.78%, and 3.70%, respectively. The pilot results suggest that the proposed GA-MBSI algorithm is potential to serve as a reliable method for noninvasive and continuous CAP estimation.

articleTitle: Monitoring muscle oxygen variations during muscle contraction in mild and severe hemiparesis using near-infrared spectroscopy: A pilot study
publicationTitle: 2019 Intelligent Rehabilitation and Human-machine Engineering Conference (IRHE-2019)
abstract: Hemiparesis is one of the most common disabling impairment in post-stroke people. However, studies on the assessment of hemiparesis have paid little attention to the metabolism status of limb muscles. In this work, a non-invasive muscle oxygenation monitoring technique, near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) was used to acquire concentration of oxy-hemoglobin (HbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) and total-hemoglobin (tHb) in four hemiparesis patients. The participants were divided into two groups. Participants who can clench their paretic side of fist were attributed to mild group and asked to perform clenching tasks using their non-paretic or paretic hand alternatively. Participants who cannot clench their paretic side of fist were attributed to severe group and asked to only perform clenching tasks using their non-paretic hand. The analysis of muscle oxygenation variation showed that the HbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and tHb decreased on the contracted side while no significant HbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and tHb changes were observed on the non-contracted side at mild group. For severe group, the HbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> contraction of the paretic side was observed to decrease when performing non-paretic fist clenching. These results indicated that the muscle oxygen variation at the paretic side was different due to the severity of hemiparesis and it may be a potential assessment for hemiparesis.

articleTitle: Analysis and prediction of multi-joint coupling torque of fingers
publicationTitle: 2019 Intelligent Rehabilitation and Human-machine Engineering Conference (IRHE-2019)
abstract: In this paper, a method of analysis and modelling of multi-joint coupling torque of finger is proposed, which can be used to predict the multi-joint coupling torque of finger in real time. Firstly, through the analysis of muscle contraction dynamics and muscle activation dynamics, the single joint neuromusculoskeletal model of finger was established, and the joint torques of metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint, proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint and distal phalangeal (DP) joint were solved. Then, the finger D-Η model was established, and the joint torques of MCP joint and PIP joint were equivalent to the point of DP joint by the principle of virtual work. The multi-joint neuromusculoskeletal model of the finger is established, and the coupling torque of the whole finger during flexion and extension is obtained. Finally, 17 parameters in the finger multi-joint neuromusculoskeletal model were identified, and data acquisition experiments were set up. The model prediction torque and software simulation torque were compared, and the root mean square error (RMSE) of the coupling torque is 0.3275, which indicates that the model has a good effect in predicting the finger joint torque and the multi-joint coupling torque.

articleTitle: Left/right contributions of articulatory muscles in speech recognition using high-density surface electromyography
publicationTitle: 2019 Intelligent Rehabilitation and Human-machine Engineering Conference (IRHE-2019)
abstract: Speaking process is one of the most important activities for human communication and it is controlled by the coordination of muscles on the face and neck. Surface electromyography (sEMG), an effective tool for detecting the electrophysiological features of muscles, was used frequently for speech recognition. Generally, the electrode position is one of the main factors impacting the classification accuracies of speech recognition. However, current sEMG-based speech recognition approaches usually depend on the electrodes chosen by experience, and whether electrodes of both left and right side should be chosen remains unclear. In this study, high-density (HD) sEMG signals were symmetrically recorded from 120 electrodes placed on both sides of the facial and neck muscles across eight normal-speaking subjects, when they were speaking five Chinese and English words, respectively. The support vector machine (SVM) classifier were applied on four time-domain features extracted from the HD sEMG signals for speech classification. The results showed that classification accuracies in speech recognition could be larger than 85% in average, and using information from the left side of the neck muscles had no significant difference from using the right side. Meanwhile, the individual difference played an import role in the left/right contributions of the facial muscles. The pilot study suggests that the left/right contributions of the articulatory muscles should be different between the neck and face, which might provide useful clue to reduce the electrode number and to select the best location of channels for speech recognition.

articleTitle: Development of a drug addiction rehabilitation training system based on BCI-VR technology
publicationTitle: 2019 Intelligent Rehabilitation and Human-machine Engineering Conference (IRHE-2019)
abstract: Since drug abuse seriously harms health of human and disturbs social stability, the anti-drug work in China remains urgent. In this paper, a drug addiction rehabilitation training system, which is based on both Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) and Virtual Reality (VR) technology is developed to help drug addicts get rid of drugs mentally. The training system is developed by 3ds Max and Unity3D, containing three different functions named as Self-Control Therapy, Aversion Therapy and Drug Craving Assessment. In Self-Control Therapy, a 3-D racing game designed for promoting the concentration of drug addicts is the key idea of the system, which achieves a real-time control through BCI technology. The communication function of the system is accomplished via UDP. The ultimate target for this system is to help drug addicts to improve their ability of self-control by repeated trainings. The system provides new ideas for drug addiction rehabilitation, and uses BCI technology rather than traditional psychological scale assessment to evaluate the real situation of drug addicts, which makes the results more persuasive.
